Rich text

Source: R/richtext.R
richtext.Rd

Marks attach a key and value (a style such as bold = TRUE, or data such as a link target) to a range of text. They merge across replicas like any other edit. As elsewhere, positions count Unicode code points and are 1-based, and a range runs from start to end.

  • text_mark() marks the characters from start to end with the marks given as key = value arguments.

  • text_unmark() removes the marks named in keys from that range.

  • text_delta() returns the text as a list of runs, each a list with a string insert and, for marked runs, a named list attributes. This is the Quill delta format. With start and end it covers only that range.

  • text_apply_delta() edits the text with a list of delta ops. Each op is a list with exactly one of retain (keep that many characters), insert (a string), or delete (remove that many characters); retain and insert may also carry attributes. An attribute set to NULL removes that mark. The output of text_delta() is itself a valid delta. A delta that reaches past the end of the text is rejected before anything is applied, but if an op fails for another reason (such as an unconfigured mark key) the ops before it stay applied.

  • doc_config_text_style() declares mark keys and how each behaves when text is inserted at the edge of a marked range.

Usage

text_mark(.text, .start, .end, ...)

text_unmark(text, start, end, keys)

text_delta(text, start = 1, end = text_length(text))

text_apply_delta(text, delta)

doc_config_text_style(.doc, ..., .default = NULL)

Arguments

.text, .start, .end

The text handle and range for text_mark(), as for text, start, and end. The argument names start with a dot so that they cannot clash with a mark key given in ....

...

For text_mark(), the marks to apply, each a plain value (see the Values section of map_set()) named with its key, for example bold = TRUE or link = "https://loro.dev". A key must not contain ":", and a value of NULL or NA removes the mark, as text_unmark() does. For doc_config_text_style(), strings giving the expand behavior of each key, for example comment = "none". Both are dynamic dots.

text

A text handle, from doc_text() or a parent container. A loro_doc is also accepted and stands for its default root container; see doc_text().

start, end

1-based positions of the first and last characters of the range. For text_delta() they default to the whole text.

keys

A character vector of mark names.

delta

A list of delta ops.

.doc

A loro_doc. The argument name starts with a dot so that it cannot clash with a mark key given in ....

.default

Expand behavior for keys that are not configured, or NULL to reject them.

Value

text_mark() returns .text invisibly, text_unmark() and text_apply_delta() return text invisibly, text_delta() returns a list, and doc_config_text_style() returns .doc invisibly.

Style configuration

A key must be configured before it can be used in a mark. New documents know these keys: bold, italic, and underline (which expand "after"), and link, highlight, comment, and code (which expand "none").

The expand behavior decides whether text inserted at a boundary of a marked range joins the mark: "after" for text inserted at its end, "before" at its start, "both", or "none".

Each call to doc_config_text_style() sets the complete configuration: the built-in keys, overridden or extended by the keys given in .... The configuration is local to a replica and is not synchronized, so every replica should configure a key the same way.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
text = doc_text(doc)
text_insert(text, 1, "Hello world")
text_mark(text, 1, 5, bold = TRUE)
text_mark(text, 7, 11, link = "https://loro.dev", italic = TRUE)
text_unmark(text, 7, 11, "italic")
str(text_delta(text))
#> List of 3
#>  $ :List of 2
#>   ..$ insert    : chr "Hello"
#>   ..$ attributes:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ bold: logi TRUE
#>  $ :List of 1
#>   ..$ insert: chr " "
#>  $ :List of 2
#>   ..$ insert    : chr "world"
#>   ..$ attributes:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ link: chr "https://loro.dev"

text_apply_delta(text, list(
  list(retain = 5),
  list(insert = ",", attributes = list(bold = TRUE)),
  list(delete = 1)
))
text_get(text)
#> [1] "Hello,world"

doc_config_text_style(doc, author = "none")
text_mark(text, 1, 5, author = "cr")
